name: Light Royal Blue
lede: Light Royal Blue is a brighter, more violet reading of [[royal-blue|Royal Blue]], a name the 2010 xkcd color survey filed rather than any dye or paint maker.

sections.title: A modifier, not a lighter royal blue
sections.body:
Despite the word "light", this xkcd entry measures darker and far more saturated than its parent, not paler: lightness 38 against Royal Blue's 48, and chroma 119 against 70 [1]. It reads closer to a pure electric violet-blue than to the deep, slightly greyed [[royal-blue|Royal Blue]], whose own name began as a dyers' grade of indigo [1]. Crowd surveys like xkcd's often use "light" loosely, as a label for a sibling shade rather than a strict lightness step [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[vibrant-blue|Vibrant Blue]], 3.0 units away and duller, with [[blurple|Purplish Blue]] close behind at 3.5, almost the same [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a color distance of 4, as photographed [2]. A blue this saturated and this close to pure electric violet-blue sits outside the range of mineral and dye pigments painters had before modern inks and screens [2].
